t: No difference was found between DMD-ASD and DMD-Control groups in the number of synonymous variants, used as a false-discovery control, indicating the RRV enrichment was specific.
DMD-ID individuals did not differ significantly from DMD-Controls in average RRV or synonymous variant counts.
No significant bias in maternal versus paternal inheritance of rare risk variants was observed in any DMD subgroup.

A pathogenic de novo nonsense variant in EBF3, associated with a monogenic autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (MIM #617330), was identified in a DMD-ASD individual (P89), constituting a dual diagnosis.

A pathogenic de novo nonsense variant in SCAF4, associated with a monogenic autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder (MIM #620511), was identified in a DMD-ASD individual (P86), constituting a dual diagnosis.

A likely pathogenic maternally inherited frameshift variant in UBE3A, associated with a monogenic neurodevelopmental disorder (MIM #105830), was identified in a DMD-ASD individual (P85), constituting a dual diagnosis.
The overall dual-diagnosis rate (dystrophinopathy plus a monogenic, highly penetrant neurodevelopmental disorder) was 8.33% in the DMD-ASD group and 0% in the DMD-ID group.
A likely pathogenic de novo variant in HEPACAM, associated with intellectual disability at low (~40%) penetrance (MIM #613926), was identified in a DMD-ID individual (P69).

Rare risk variants identified in DMD-ASD and DMD-ID individuals were significantly enriched in genes related to extracellular matrix (ECM) constituents, collagen fibril/trimer components, integrin and non-integrin cell-surface interactions, collagen trimerization, and syndecan interactions, and were enriched for Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome gene associations; no such enrichment was found in the DMD-Control group.

The authors cite prior literature indicating that individuals with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome and hypermobility syndrome are at increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders, including ASD, though the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

The authors propose that combined disruption of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex (DGC), which links ECM to intracellular components, together with insults in ECM components (including collagen genes), elevates ASD risk in dystrophinopathies.
Patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome are reported to be at increased risk for ligamentous instability and for intraoperative and postoperative complications.
In a cited study of EDS patients undergoing surgical treatment, wound complications occurred in 11% and infection occurred in 6% of patients.

A 16-year-old gymnast with EDS and Chiari I malformation sustained a lateral collateral ligament tear of the hallux interphalangeal joint with increased joint laxity following hyperextension trauma during gymnastics.
Conservative treatment (CAM boot, RICE, NSAIDs) failed to resolve symptoms, leading to surgical repair of the torn lateral collateral ligament using suture anchors and Kirschner wire fixation.

Six weeks after surgical repair, the patient developed a draining sinus/wound complication attributed to the nonabsorbable suture paired with the absorbable suture anchor, requiring an additional incision and drainage procedure.

Following revision incision and drainage with excision of the sinus tract and removal of the offending suture, joint stability of the lateral collateral ligament repair was confirmed intraoperatively by varus stress testing under fluoroscopy.
In an unadjusted model, generalised joint hypermobility (GJH) was significantly associated with increased odds of not fully recovering from COVID-19.
After adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, education, and vaccination status/number, GJH remained a significant independent predictor of non-recovery from COVID-19.
GJH was significantly associated with higher fatigue levels after adjusting for covariates.

Fatigue levels statistically mediated the relationship between GJH and non-recovery from COVID-19, suggesting fatigue as a mechanistic pathway linking connective tissue variance to persistent COVID symptoms.
GJH was not significantly associated with the likelihood of reporting a COVID-19 infection in the first place.
A higher proportion of participants who had not recovered from COVID-19 had GJH compared with those who had fully recovered.
A prior cited study by the same authors found that the majority of patients with fibromyalgia and ME/CFS also had symptomatic joint hypermobility, though most had not been previously diagnosed.
A cited large cohort study found fibromyalgia to be among the strongest pre-existing condition risk factors for developing long COVID.
Whole exome sequencing identified a mutation in AHDC1 consistent with Xia Gibbs Syndrome in a boy who had developed Autism Spectrum Disorder.
Joint hypermobility was identified during pediatric neurology consultation prompted by the patient's dysmorphic appearance, as part of the Xia Gibbs Syndrome phenotype.

The patient showed regression of previously acquired cognitive skills between ages 4 and 4.5, with loss of joint attention, emergence of stereotypic movements, and limited eye contact, culminating in an Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis.
The patient's initial presentation at age 2 was speech delay, which was later followed by a diagnosis of cognitive retardation.

Across the 12 included studies, elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α) and CRP were reported in the majority of studies as a shared biomarker signature linking fibromyalgia, depression, and autoimmune diseases.
Serotonin dysregulation, mediated in part by altered platelet function, was implicated as a mechanism linking inflammation, mood disturbance, and pain perception in fibromyalgia and depression.

Autoantibodies isolated from fibromyalgia patients and passively transferred to animal models induced pain hypersensitivity, reduced grip strength, and muscle weakness, implicating a peripheral autoimmune mechanism in fibromyalgia.
The HPA axis is proposed as a central mediator linking psychological stress, immune dysfunction, and heightened pain sensitivity across fibromyalgia, depression, and autoimmune disease.
Pro-inflammatory cytokines can activate the HPA axis and promote glucocorticoid production, perpetuating neuroinflammatory processes that contribute to the neurobiological burden of depression.

Chronic inflammation observed in autoimmune diseases such as SLE and multiple sclerosis predisposes patients to depression via continuous exposure of the brain to inflammatory mediators, forming a bidirectional inflammation-depression feedback loop.

Low-dose IL-2 therapy showed preliminary antidepressant effects, particularly in treatment-resistant major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder, potentially via restoring T-regulatory cell balance.
N-acetylcysteine demonstrated promise in reducing depressive symptoms and systemic inflammation in individuals with elevated cytokine levels, by modulating oxidative stress and cytokine production.
Minocycline demonstrated promise in reducing depressive symptoms and systemic inflammation in individuals with elevated cytokine levels, via modulation of neuroinflammatory processes.

TNF-α inhibitors and IL-6 modulators are being explored as adjunctive treatments for depressive disorders associated with chronic inflammation and may be suited to patients with elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines.

Aberrant antibodies in fibromyalgia appear to target specific sensory nerves, producing heightened pain perception and sensory abnormalities, indicating a peripheral immune component alongside central sensitization.
Baseline stress levels correlated positively with pain intensity scores in fibromyalgia and other chronic widespread pain conditions in a long-term longitudinal study.
Stress and pain catastrophizing showed strong positive correlations with pain severity and co-occurrence of multiple painful conditions.
IL-6, norepinephrine, and resting heart rate were suggested as predictors of chronic low back pain, another chronic primary pain condition influenced by psychosocial stressors.
Psychopathological profile, stress and coping-mechanism differences are associated with fibromyalgia symptoms and reduced pain threshold.
Mindfulness combined with exercise to reduce stress level was effective for chronic pain.
The Trier Social Stress Test, an acute psychosocial stress task, decreased both thermo- and mechanonociceptive thresholds, producing hyperalgesia and allodynia in fibromyalgia patients.
A higher percentage of mood disorders are present in fibromyalgia patients compared to the healthy population.
In women, pain severity and catastrophizing were associated with higher depression and anxiety levels.
Cognitive behavior therapy as a stress management method significantly improved coping and self-reported depression ratings in fibromyalgia patients.

Increased uptake of the [11C]PBR28 PET radioligand, which binds the translocator protein expressed by activated microglia/astrocytes, was found in the prefrontal cortex of fibromyalgia patients and positively correlated with fatigue symptoms.
Choline levels linked to glial activation were elevated in several brain areas of fibromyalgia patients, positively correlating with pain parameters, as assessed by fMRI.

Functional connectivity within the salience network was increased in participants exposed to chronic psychosocial stressors compared to unexposed participants, suggesting neuroplasticity-related network reorganization.
Increased salience network connectivity observed in PTSD patients normalized after evidence-based psychotherapy.
Enhanced default mode network connectivity was observed in fibromyalgia patients and positively correlated with pain intensity.
A meta-analysis demonstrated gray matter abnormalities in chronic primary pain patients.
Neuroinflammation detected with the PK11195 PET tracer in different brain areas of fibromyalgia and CRPS patients showed distribution volume ratios that correlated with stress and anxiety levels.
Chronic stress paradigms in rats activated microglia, shown by increased Iba1 immunoreactivity density in the medial prefrontal cortex.
Chronic restraint stress caused loss of neural dendritic spines in the medial amygdala in mice.
In the acid saline fibromyalgia mouse model, default mode network-periaqueductal gray matter functional connectivity showed the strongest positive correlation with pain threshold decrease.
In the reserpine-induced rat fibromyalgia model, moderate electrical forepaw stimulation induced significantly higher default mode network activation compared to controls.
Systemic injection of purified IgG antibodies from fibromyalgia patients bound to satellite glia cells in the dorsal root ganglia and induced severe symptoms including hyperalgesia in a mouse model.

Passive transfer of fibromyalgia patients' IgG mimicked mechanical hyperalgesia, reduced grip strength, reduced locomotor activity and increased nociceptor excitability in mice, with increased GFAP expression in lumbar dorsal root ganglia but not the spinal dorsal horn.

Fibromyalgia patients had lower circulating NGF and IL-1β but higher BDNF and IL-8 compared to healthy controls, though these biomarkers did not correlate with depressive/anxiety symptoms, pain-catastrophizing, or pain levels.
Chronic restraint stress activated the NLRP3 inflammasome in the hippocampus and basolateral amygdala of rats.
Reducing hippocampal chronic-restraint-stress-induced proBDNF upregulation resulted in reduced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in rats.
Chronic variable mild stress-induced thermal hyperalgesia could be prevented by blocking BDNF signaling.

Psychological distress, pain intensity and sensitivity in fibromyalgia patients showed positive correlations with plasma proteins involved in inflammation and immunity including IL-6, IL-2, and haptoglobin.
Inflammatory response proteins were detected in fibromyalgia patients' cerebrospinal fluid by proteomic analysis, suggesting inflammatory and neuroendocrine disturbances.

Female fibromyalgia patients' isolated monocytes secreted higher levels of IL-1, IL-5, IL-6 and IL-10 compared to healthy controls, with IL-4, IL-5 and IL-10 positively correlating with pain intensity and related mood disturbances.
Increased serum levels of tachykinins substance P and hemokinin-1 were detected in fibromyalgia patients compared to controls, and these decreased following cognitive behavior therapy.
Hemokinin-1 deficiency prevented chronic-restraint-stress-induced hyperalgesia in both male and female mice.

Chronic restraint stress-induced hyperalgesia and associated astroglia/microglia activation in stress- and pain-related brain regions did not develop in mice lacking IL-1, indicating IL-1's importance in this pain sensitization mechanism.

PET imaging using the microglial/astrocyte marker [11C]-(R)-PK11195 revealed neuroinflammation in multiple brain regions of both fibromyalgia and CRPS patients, with distribution volume ratio correlating with stress and anxiety levels.
Chronic stress activates microglia and astrocytes, demonstrated in animal experiments more than two decades ago.
Chronic stress paradigms in rats activated microglia, shown by increased Iba1 immunoreactivity density in the medial prefrontal cortex.
Chronic restraint stress caused loss of neural dendritic spines in the medial amygdala in mice.
Brain-derived neurotrophic factor is suggested to mediate remodeling and neuroplasticity changes in brain areas affected by chronic stress in mice.
Animal models of chronic stress showed deteriorated salience network connectivity, paralleling human findings.
In the acid saline mouse model of fibromyalgia, default mode network–periaqueductal gray functional connectivity showed the strongest positive correlation with decreased pain threshold.
In the reserpine-induced rat fibromyalgia model, moderate electrical forepaw stimulation induced significantly higher default mode network activation compared to controls.

Systemic injection of purified IgG from fibromyalgia patients bound to satellite glia cells in dorsal root ganglia and induced severe symptoms including hyperalgesia in a mouse model, supporting an autoimmune mechanism.
Passive transfer of fibromyalgia patients' IgG into mice mimicked mechanical hyperalgesia, reduced grip strength and locomotor activity, and increased nociceptor excitability.

In the passive-transfer IgG model, GFAP expression increased in the lumbar dorsal root ganglia at the level of primary sensory neurons but not in the spinal dorsal horn at the level of secondary sensory neurons.
Fibromyalgia patients had lower circulating levels of NGF and IL-1β than healthy controls.
Fibromyalgia patients had higher circulating BDNF and IL-8 levels than healthy controls.
No correlation was found between NGF, IL-1β, BDNF, and IL-8 levels and fibromyalgia patients' depressive/anxiety symptoms, pain-catastrophizing, or pain levels.
Chronic restraint stress in rats activated the NLRP3 inflammasome in the hippocampus and basolateral amygdala, accompanied by increased expression of the neuronal activation marker c-fos and IL-1β.
Reducing hippocampal chronic-restraint-stress-induced proBDNF upregulation resulted in reduced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in rats.
Blocking BDNF signaling prevented chronic-variable-mild-stress-induced thermal hyperalgesia in an animal model.
Psychological distress, pain intensity, and pain sensitivity in fibromyalgia patients showed positive correlations with plasma inflammatory/immune proteins including IL-6, IL-2, and haptoglobin.
Proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid from fibromyalgia patients detected inflammatory response proteins, suggesting inflammatory and neuroendocrine disturbances.

Repeated swim stress, intermittent cold stress, sound stress combined with bradykinin injection, and chronic immobilization stress all induce mechanical and thermal hyper-nociception in rodents similar to that seen in fibromyalgia patients.
Chronic variable mild stress is an appropriate model of depression but is not suitable for investigating stress-induced pain mechanisms relevant to fibromyalgia.
Systemic reserpine injection, which depletes monoamines, mimics spontaneous pain and thermal and mechanical hyperalgesia in a rodent fibromyalgia model.
Acid saline injection into the gastrocnemius muscle results in mechanical hypersensitivity in rodents, though the development of thermal sensitivity in this model remains debated.

In the passive-transfer IgG mouse model of fibromyalgia, GFAP expression increased specifically in the lumbar dorsal root ganglia at the level of primary sensory neurons, but not in the spinal dorsal horn at the level of secondary sensory neurons.

Concentrations of IL-4, IL-5 and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 secreted by monocytes showed positive correlations with pain intensity and related mood disturbances in female fibromyalgia patients.

Stress-induced elevation of IL-1 in both brain homogenates and plasma samples was absent in fractalkine receptor (CX3CR1)-deleted mice, implicating microglial fractalkine receptor activation in IL-1 release upon chronic stress.
Fibromyalgia patients had lower circulating levels of NGF and IL-1β compared to healthy controls.

Fibromyalgia patients had higher circulating levels of BDNF and IL-8 compared to healthy controls, though these biomarkers did not correlate with depressive/anxiety symptoms, pain-catastrophizing, or pain levels.
Fremanezumab treatment produced a significant reduction in monthly headache days over the first three months compared with pre-treatment baseline.
Overall, 61.8% of patients achieved a ≥50% reduction in headache days, 27.0% achieved ≥75%, and only 2 patients achieved a 100% response.
Patients who had previously failed both erenumab and galcanezumab had a markedly lower response rate to fremanezumab than CGRP-antibody-naive patients.
Response rate to fremanezumab differed by which single prior CGRP antibody had failed: patients who had failed erenumab responded better than those who had failed galcanezumab.
Longer HF/CM disease duration was strongly associated with poorer response to fremanezumab.
Patients with HF/CM duration ≤6 years had a substantially higher fremanezumab response rate than those with longer duration.
Patients with high-frequency episodic migraine (HF) responded better to fremanezumab than patients with chronic migraine (CM).
Almost daily headaches (≥28 days/month) was the strongest predictor of poor fremanezumab response.
Analgesic (medication) overuse was associated with a significantly lower fremanezumab response rate.
Comorbid anxiety-depression was significantly associated with reduced response to fremanezumab and remained an independent predictor on multivariate analysis.
Comorbid fibromyalgia was associated with a significantly lower response rate to fremanezumab in migraine patients, though this did not remain independently significant after multivariate adjustment.
Multivariate logistic regression identified almost-daily headaches, HF/CM duration exceeding six years, and anxiety-depression as independent predictors of poor fremanezumab response.
Age was significantly different between univariate responders and non-responders, but this effect disappeared after multivariate adjustment for disease duration.
Sex was not significantly associated with fremanezumab response, although women showed a numerically higher response rate than men.
Presence of migraine aura did not significantly modify response to fremanezumab.
Fremanezumab was well tolerated with only mild adverse events and no serious adverse events or infusion reactions reported.
Fremanezumab treatment was associated with a reduction in the rate of medication overuse from baseline to the first treatment quarter.
The PPAR-γ agonist pioglitazone significantly reduced β-hexosaminidase release from RBL-2H3 mast cells activated by FcεRI cross-linking.
PIO treatment lowered mRNA expression levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines induced by FcεRI cross-linking in RBL-2H3 cells.
A total of 24 differentially expressed genes (15 up-regulated, 9 down-regulated) were identified in RBL-2H3 cells treated with PIO versus untreated cells.

GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses showed that immune system, signal transduction, infectious disease, and signaling molecules and interactions were the most enriched annotation categories among DEGs.
Protein-protein interaction network analysis showed that most identified DEGs interacted with PPAR-γ.
PPAR-γ agonist treatment activated both PPAR-γ and NRF2 signaling pathways in resting RBL-2H3 cells.
Protein expression of PPAR-γ was greatly upregulated in RBL-2H3 cells activated via FcεRI aggregation.
Protein expression of Cpt1a was greatly upregulated in RBL-2H3 cells activated via FcεRI aggregation.
Protein expression of Acsl4 was greatly upregulated in RBL-2H3 cells activated via FcεRI aggregation.
The inhibitory effect of the PPAR-γ agonist pioglitazone on degranulation of FcεRI-activated RBL-2H3 cells was shown to be dependent on PPAR-γ itself.
PPAR-γ agonism reduced phosphorylation levels of FcεRI-mediated signaling molecules in RBL-2H3 cells in a PPAR-γ-dependent manner.
A genome-wide significant association was found between the MHC locus and SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG antibody titer in the discovery cohort, replicated in the independent replication cohort.

A genome-wide significant association was found between the IGH locus and SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG antibody titer in the discovery cohort, with the effect allele decreasing titers, replicated in the independent replication cohort.
A population-specific missense variant in IGHG1 (p.Leu192Val), common in East Asians but rare elsewhere, strongly decreases SARS-CoV-2 vaccine-induced IgG antibody titer.

The MHC lead variant was also associated with increased antibody titers against influenza B/Yamagata both before and after influenza vaccination, indicating shared genetic determinants of antibody responses across vaccine types.

The IGH missense variant rs1043109 significantly decreased antibody titers against influenza B/Victoria and B/Yamagata, suggesting the IGH variant broadly affects acute IgG production beyond SARS-CoV-2.

Fine-mapping identified HLA-DRβ1 amino acid position 96 as the top MHC class II variant associated with COVID-19 vaccine IgG titer in Japanese, distinct from HLA-DQB1*06 and HLA-DRβ1 position 71 reported in European studies, and it explained 3.1% of antibody titer variance.
In the UK Biobank, GWAS of COVID-19 vaccine IgG serostatus identified four genome-wide significant loci: IGK (2p11), MHC (6p21), IGH (14q32), and a novel 16p11 locus.
The IGK serostatus-associated variant rs139861548 is an eQTL that upregulates IGKV1-13 gene expression, with strong colocalization evidence linking gene expression and antibody serostatus.
The MHC locus showed genome-wide significant association with SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell response levels against both antigen 1 and antigen 2, replicated in the independent cohort.
The IGH IgG-titer-associated variant rs1043109 showed no association with SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell response levels, indicating distinct genetic architectures for humoral versus cellular immunity.
Fine-mapping of T cell response identified HLA-DRβ1 positions 47 and 13 and an independent HLA-DPB1*03:01 allele as significant contributors, together explaining 14.5% of T cell response variance.
The effect size of the European IGH-IgG serostatus association waned over time after vaccination, from β = −0.13 at 3 weeks to β = −0.051 at 6 months.
The IgG antibody titer HLA genetic score was associated with 15 circulating proteins, including 8 trans-associated immune proteins such as LILRB4 and FCRL6, encoded outside the MHC locus.
The European IGH serostatus variant showed significant trans-pQTL associations, decreasing ARHGAP5 and RGS8 protein levels and increasing DNAJB8 levels.
The European 16p11 IgG serostatus-associated variant had an increasing cis-pQTL effect on SULT1A1 protein levels.
Among autosomal expanded mCA classes, Any14q and Any6p showed the strongest associations with COVID-19 IgG antibody serostatus, coinciding with the germline IGH and MHC GWAS loci.

Expanded hematopoietic mosaic chromosomal alterations affecting the IGH locus were associated with markedly reduced vaccine-induced antibody production, an effect robust to exclusion of immunosuppressed individuals.
All carriers of MHC-affecting expanded mosaic chromosomal alterations were seronegative for anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG at least one week post-vaccination, in contrast to non-MHC-affecting 6p mCA carriers.
MHC-affecting expanded mCA events conferred increased risk of infectious diseases of multiple organ systems (eye/ear/mastoid, respiratory, skin) in BioBank Japan.
In elderly UK Biobank participants, MHC-affecting expanded mCA events conferred substantially increased risk of respiratory infection and sepsis.
IGH-affecting expanded mCA events conferred increased risk of sepsis in both BioBank Japan and UK Biobank cohorts.
Both MHC-affecting and IGH-affecting expanded mCA events increased risk of Graves' disease in elderly BioBank Japan participants, with a concordant direction in UK Biobank for IGH.
Expanded mLOY (cell fraction >10%) in males showed a negative association with SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibody serostatus, while expanded mLOX in females showed no significant association.
Expanded mLOX (cell fraction >10%) in females conferred increased risk of Graves' disease and rheumatoid arthritis in BioBank Japan, particularly among the elderly.
Expanded mLOY (cell fraction >5%) in males conferred increased risk of asthma and rheumatoid arthritis in both BioBank Japan and UK Biobank.
Reduced CFTR chloride channel function can compromise intestinal epithelial barrier integrity, allowing microbial antigens to penetrate tissue and trigger excessive immune responses in IBD.

ClC-2, expressed in mast cells and epithelial cells, supports tight junction integrity and reduces intestinal permeability, and its dysregulation is linked to altered mast cell activity and excessive pro-inflammatory mediator release.
Dysregulation of chloride channels in mast cells is linked to altered mast cell activation, degranulation, cytokine release, and immune cell recruitment in inflamed IBD tissue.

Pharmacological strategies targeting chloride channels, including CFTR potentiators and ClC-2 activators, show potential to mitigate inflammatory responses in IBD, though achieving specificity and minimizing side effects remain challenges.

Intersection of differentially expressed genes with a curated list of 1,596 oxidative stress-related genes identified 13 oxidative stress-related differentially expressed genes (OSRDEGs) distinguishing keloid from normal skin tissue.
EDN1 expression was significantly upregulated in keloid tissue relative to normal skin across the combined training datasets, with moderate diagnostic accuracy (AUC=0.850).
NTF3 expression was significantly upregulated in keloid tissue relative to normal skin across the combined training datasets, with high diagnostic accuracy (AUC=0.940).
WGCNA identified brown and blue gene co-expression modules that were significantly correlated with fibrosis and inflammation phenotypes in keloid tissue.
EDN1 and NTF3 were identified as hub genes with high connectivity centrally located within the fibrosis/inflammation-associated WGCNA modules.
EDN1 and NTF3 expression were significantly positively correlated with fibrosis markers (COL1A1, TGFB1) and inflammatory factors (IL6, TNFA) in keloid tissue.
GSEA showed significant enrichment of the IL-18 signaling pathway in keloid tissue relative to normal skin.
GSEA showed significant enrichment of the IL-23 signaling pathway in keloid tissue relative to normal skin.
EDN1 expression showed the strongest positive correlation with activated mast cell infiltration among all immune cell types examined in keloid tissue.
NTF3 expression showed the strongest negative correlation with resting mast cell infiltration in keloid tissue, suggesting a role in promoting mast cell activation.
NTF3 showed a significant positive correlation with activated mast cells in an independent validation dataset (GSE7890), consistent with the training datasets.
In the independent validation dataset GSE7890, EDN1 upregulation was replicated but NTF3 upregulation did not reach statistical significance, likely due to small validation sample size.
qPCR analysis of patient tissue confirmed significantly increased mRNA expression of both EDN1 and NTF3 in keloid tissue compared to normal skin.
Immunohistochemistry showed markedly increased EDN1 and NTF3 protein staining in fibrotic, collagen-dense regions and fibroblast-like cells of keloid dermis compared to normal skin.

The endothelin receptor antagonist bosentan is discussed as a candidate therapeutic to inhibit fibroblast activity and ECM deposition via the EDN1 pathway, based on evidence from other fibrotic diseases, warranting future evaluation in keloid models.
Drug-gene interaction analysis using the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database predicted valproic acid as an interactor of NTF3, proposed as a potential therapeutic target in keloid.

In single-gene functional enrichment analysis of a candidate cellular-senescence biomarker gene identified from AMI blood transcriptome data, ATP6V0B (which was overexpressed in AMI vs control samples) was significantly enriched among GO terms including 'mast cell activation', alongside other immune-related terms.
Administration of a 500-mL crystalloid fluid bolus produced a statistically significant increase in systolic blood pressure in acute ischemic stroke patients.
The crystalloid bolus produced a statistically significant increase in stroke volume index in acute ischemic stroke patients.

Despite significant increases in blood pressure and stroke volume index after the fluid bolus, the mean flow velocity of the ipsilateral middle cerebral artery measured by transcranial Doppler did not change significantly.

In an exploratory multivariable linear regression adjusting for age, baseline stroke volume index, and systolic blood pressure, no factors were significantly associated with the change in mean flow velocity after the fluid bolus.
Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, caused by mutation in the collagen type III alpha 1 chain gene (COL3A1), is listed among the clinically significant syndromic causes of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm.
COL3A1 mutation causing Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is also listed among the monogenic Mendelian causes of intracranial aneurysm.

COL3A1, the EDS-associated collagen gene, is among 24 genes identified as overlapping between thoracic aortic aneurysm (70 candidate genes) and intracranial aneurysm (88 candidate genes) gene lists, falling within the shared extracellular matrix organization pathway.
Tympanic (core body) temperature was higher in postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia compared to postmenopausal healthy controls.
Hand skin temperature (both hands) differed significantly between healthy premenopausal women and premenopausal women with fibromyalgia, consistent with excessive peripheral vasodilation in FM.

Hand skin temperature (both hands) also differed significantly between healthy postmenopausal women and postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia, indicating FM independently increases hand skin temperature regardless of menopausal status.
No differences were found in hand, axillary, or tympanic temperature, or serum NO levels between healthy premenopausal and healthy postmenopausal women.

No differences were found in hand, axillary, or tympanic temperature, or serum NO levels between premenopausal and postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia, suggesting menopause does not alter these parameters in FM patients.
Two-week rapamycin treatment significantly increased cytokeratin-18 abundance in the proximal thoracic aorta of Marfan mgR/mgR mice compared to sham.
Rapamycin treatment increased the abundance of betaglycan (TGF-β type 3 receptor, TGFBR3) in the aortic wall of mgR/mgR mice.
Rapamycin raised the abundance of ADAMTS5 (aggrecanase-2), an enzyme involved in ECM remodelling, in the mgR/mgR mouse aorta.
Rapamycin raised the abundance of xylosyltransferase-1, an enzyme involved in ECM remodelling and homeostasis, in the mgR/mgR mouse aorta.

Rapamycin, an mTOR pathway inhibitor, limits ascending aorta elastolysis and expansion and significantly increases lifespan in the mgR/mgR Marfan mouse model, as previously demonstrated by the authors.

Direct contact co-culture of AMSCs with SSc skin fibroblasts (ratios 1:5 and 1:10) reduced mRNA and protein levels of α-SMA, COL3A1, and TGF-β1 compared with fibroblasts alone, with the 1:5 ratio showing the strongest inhibitory effect.

Indirect (transwell) co-culture of AMSCs with SSc skin fibroblasts reduced mRNA and protein expression of α-SMA, COL1A1, COL3A1, and TGF-β1, with efficacy independent of AMSC cell number, implicating paracrine secretion.
PKH67-labeled AMSC-derived exosomes co-localized with fibroblast nuclei after 24h incubation, demonstrating that exosomes are successfully internalized by SSc skin fibroblasts.
Treatment of SSc skin fibroblasts with AMSC-derived exosomes (3 µg/mL) for 48h inhibited mRNA and protein expression of α-SMA, COL1A1, and COL3A1.
AMSC-derived exosomes (3 µg/mL) significantly inhibited the classical TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling pathway in SSc skin fibroblasts.

Bleomycin (BLM)-induced SSc model mice showed significantly increased dermal thickness, collagen content, and α-SMA/COL3A1 protein expression compared with saline-treated controls, validating the fibrosis model.
BLM-treated mice showed a significant decrease in body weight compared with controls during the 4-week modeling period, though no mice died.

Subcutaneous treatment with AMSCs or AMSC-derived exosomes reduced dermal thickness, collagen volume fraction, and α-SMA/COL3A1 protein expression in BLM-induced SSc mouse skin compared with untreated BLM mice.
The TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling pathway was upregulated in BLM-induced SSc model mouse skin compared with control.
AMSCs and AMSC-derived exosome treatment inhibited the upregulated TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling axis in BLM-induced SSc mouse skin, suggesting exosomes ameliorate skin fibrosis via this pathway.

Cited prior work (Nakamura et al.) found increased mRNA levels and exosome secretion of exosomal markers CD63, CD9, and CD81 in skin samples and dermal fibroblasts from SSc patients compared with controls.

Cited prior work (Wermuth et al.) reported that four pro-fibrotic miRNAs were upregulated ~5-fold and four anti-fibrotic miRNAs were downregulated ~70-fold in serum exosomes from SSc patients compared with normal subjects.
Cited prior work (Rozier et al.) found that AMSC-derived extracellular vesicles had a stronger antifibrotic effect than AMSCs themselves in an in vitro TGF-β1-induced SSc fibroblast model.

Biologic therapies such as the CD80/CD86 blockers abatacept and tocilizumab, along with most RCTs targeting skin fibrosis in SSc, failed to meet their primary endpoint of reducing the Modified Rodnan Skin Score.
CSF transferrin levels were significantly lower in Lewy body disease patients compared to controls.
CSF orosomucoid levels were significantly lower in Lewy body disease patients compared to controls.
CSF C3 complement levels were significantly lower in Lewy body disease patients compared to controls, likely reflecting complement activation and consumption.
Serum β2 microglobulin was significantly decreased in Lewy body disease patients compared to controls.
The CSF/serum quotient of transferrin was significantly lower in Lewy body disease patients than in controls, suggesting BBB or transport disruption.
The CSF/serum quotient of C3 complement was significantly lower in Lewy body disease patients than in controls.
CSF transferrin, C3 complement, C4 complement and orosomucoid were all significantly lower in MSA patients compared to controls.
The CSF/serum quotient of transferrin was significantly lower in MSA patients compared to controls.
None of the six inflammatory biomarkers or their CSF/serum quotients showed significant differences between 4-repeat tauopathy (PSP/CBS) patients and controls.
Serum C3 complement was significantly lower in both LBD and MSA (synucleinopathies) compared to 4RT (tauopathy), suggesting distinct pathology-specific inflammatory responses.
Serum orosomucoid showed a strong non-significant trend towards lower levels in LBD compared to 4RT.
CSF haptoglobin showed a non-significant trend towards lower levels in LBD patients compared to controls (p = 0.053).

A logistic regression model combining all six biomarkers plus age and sex covariates explained 55.8% of variation and correctly predicted 76.1% of cases distinguishing LBD from controls, with C3 complement and age as the largest contributors.

A logistic regression model combining all biomarkers plus covariates explained 54.1% of variation and correctly predicted 85.9% of cases distinguishing MSA from controls, with C3 complement, serum orosomucoid, and age as largest contributors.

A logistic regression model combining all biomarkers plus covariates explained 61.5% of variation and correctly predicted 90.5% of cases distinguishing 4RT from controls, with haptoglobin, serum C3 complement, and age as largest contributors.

Both age and sex significantly influence most CSF biomarker levels and CSF/serum quotients, while among serum biomarkers only C3 complement (sex) and β2M (age) were significantly affected by covariates.

CSF concentrations of all six biomarkers were reduced across all three neurodegenerative groups (LBD, MSA, 4RT) relative to controls, though changes were only moderate and reached significance mainly in LBD and MSA, with no significance in 4RT; serum changes were less uniform, with a preferential decrease in LBD/MSA and slight increase in 4RT.
In the 10 years before the DanFunD study, individuals with functional somatic disorder (FSD) used on average 3.9 more weeks per year of sickness benefit than those without FSD.
In the 10 years before the DanFunD study, individuals with FSD used on average 1.3 more weeks per year of unemployment benefit than those without FSD.
In the 10 years before the DanFunD study, individuals with FSD used on average 3.8 more weeks per year of disability pension than those without FSD.
The elevated welfare benefit use among individuals with FSD persisted in the 4 years after the DanFunD study and was also seen among those diagnosed via diagnostic interview.
Individuals with questionnaire-defined FSD had higher welfare benefit use than individuals with other severe physical diseases.

Manual acupuncture at ST36 produced a transient reduction in blood pressure, heart rate, left ventricular end-systolic pressure, and +dp/dtmax and -dp/dtmin, indicating negative inotropic and chronotropic effects.
Manual acupuncture at the control acupoint PC6 (Neiguan) did not significantly alter blood pressure, heart rate, or cardiac contractility, in contrast to ST36.
MA at ST36 significantly increased local blood perfusion in both the ipsilateral and contralateral groin regions as measured by laser speckle contrast imaging.

Echocardiography showed that MA at ST36 transiently decreased velocity time integral (VTI) of the femoral artery and cardiac stroke volume, both returning to baseline within 5 minutes after acupuncture cessation.
MA at ST39 augmented ipsilateral groin blood perfusion but, unlike ST36, did not increase contralateral perfusion, indicating acupoint-specific systemic vasodilatory effects.

Following ST36 stimulation, heart rate variability analysis showed a significant increase in LF power, a decrease in HF power, and an increased LF/HF ratio, indicating a shift toward greater sympathetic relative to parasympathetic activity.
RMSSD, a time-domain HRV parameter, showed no statistically significant change after ST36 stimulation.

Western blot analysis of ventricular tissue showed no significant change in AChE or total TH, but phosphorylated TH (p-TH) was significantly elevated and the p-TH/TH ratio showed a near-significant increase after MA at ST36, suggesting increased sympathetic activation.

RNA-seq of ST36 acupoint skin identified 800 differentially expressed genes (515 upregulated, 285 downregulated) versus control, with many involved in inflammation, including chemokines (Ccl2, Ccl22, Cxcl1, Cxcl2), interleukins (Il1b, Il10ra, Il17re, Il1rl1), and nitric oxide synthase isoforms (Nos1, Nos2, Nostrin).

KEGG and GSEA pathway analyses of DEGs from ST36-stimulated tissue showed enrichment of TNF signaling pathway, IL-17 signaling pathway, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction among the top pathways.
Serum TNF-α levels were significantly elevated after MA at ST36 compared with control, whereas local TNF-α expression at the acupoint site showed only a modest, non-significant increase of 12%.
ELISA results showed reduced serum TGF-β and IL-1β levels after MA at ST36 compared with control, contrasting with the elevated TNF-α response.

Intravenous administration of the non-selective NOS inhibitor L-NAME abolished the ST36-induced hypotensive effect, while saline control did not, and the reduction in mean arterial pressure was substantially greater in the L-NAME group than the saline group, implicating NO as a mediator of acupuncture-induced hypotension.

Transcriptomic and pharmacological data together support a model in which ST36 stimulation induces local inflammation that upregulates iNOS (Nos2), increasing NO production and mediating the observed hypotensive and vasodilatory effects, with possible contribution from eNOS activation via shear stress.
Patients with sleep-related stridor onset within 3 years of disease onset had a shorter disease duration than those with later stridor onset.
Patients with early stridor onset had a higher age at disease onset than those with late stridor onset.
Patients with early stridor onset more frequently had autonomic symptoms as the presenting feature of MSA compared to those with late stridor onset.
In the univariate Cox regression, early stridor onset (within 3 years) was associated with increased risk of death.
In the univariate Cox regression, early RBD onset (within 3 years) was associated with increased risk of death.
In the multivariable Cox model adjusted for autonomic onset and age at disease onset, early stridor onset remained an independent predictor of mortality.
In the same multivariable Cox model, early RBD onset also remained an independent predictor of mortality.

Early symptomatic orthostatic hypotension, urinary urgency/frequency, urinary retention, and urinary incontinence, autonomic onset, and older age at onset were all associated with increased mortality risk in univariate Cox regression.
CSF neurofilament light chain levels were not significantly associated with survival in univariate Cox regression.
MSA patients with early stridor and/or RBD onset had higher CSF neurofilament light chain levels than patients with late onset of both stridor and RBD.
In the stridor-only subgroup, patients with early stridor onset showed a trend toward higher CSF NfL than those with late stridor onset, but the difference was not statistically significant.

Patients with early stridor onset reached major disability milestones (frequent falls, urinary catheterization, unintelligible speech, dysphagia/PEG, wheelchair dependency) significantly sooner than patients with late stridor onset.
Patients with combined early stridor and/or RBD onset reached all five disability milestones significantly sooner than those with late onset of both stridor and RBD.
Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a higher risk of death in patients with early stridor onset compared to late stridor onset, with a higher death incidence rate.
Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a higher risk of death in patients with early RBD onset compared to late RBD onset.
Kaplan-Meier analysis combining stridor and RBD showed a higher risk of death in patients with early onset of either sleep disorder compared to those with late onset of both.
The sex distribution differed between MSA patients with early stridor/RBD onset (more balanced) and those with late onset (more male-predominant).

The authors propose that early co-occurrence of stridor, RBD and autonomic dysfunction reflects a common pathogenic pathway involving degeneration of interconnected brainstem nuclei controlling sleep, cardiovascular control and respiration.

The dysautonomia symptom domain (28 distinct standardized reported symptoms spanning GI, genitourinary, and cardiovascular systems) was assessed in the majority of both prodromal and early motor Parkinson's disease cohorts.

In prodromal PD cohorts, constipation was the most frequently reported autonomic symptom, followed by hyperhidrosis, sexual dysfunction, orthostatic symptoms, and urinary symptoms/sialorrhea/dysphagia.
In early motor PD cohorts, constipation, urinary symptoms, sexual dysfunction, dysphagia, and sialorrhea were the most frequently reported autonomic symptoms.
In one gender-stratified early motor PD study, men reported more sexual dysfunction symptoms while women reported more behavioral symptoms such as depression.
In another gender-stratified study, men were more prone to developing drooling and nocturia than women, regardless of dopaminergic treatment status.

The MDS-UPDRS parts Ib+II, NMSS, and SCOPA-AUT were the most commonly used tools to capture autonomic symptoms in early motor PD cohorts, whereas interviews, questionnaires, and medical record review predominated in prodromal PD cohorts.

Pain was one of the most frequently reported sensory symptoms in both prodromal and early motor PD, suggesting it may be an intrinsic feature of PD pathophysiology rather than purely secondary to motor symptoms.

Hyposmia was the most prominent sensory symptom in prodromal PD, reported in roughly half of prodromal cohorts and remaining highly prevalent in early motor PD, consistent with its established role as an early biomarker.
REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) was the most studied sleep-domain symptom in prodromal PD cohorts, reported in 40% of prodromal cohorts.

The review synthesized a conceptual model organizing patient-reported experiences of prodromal and early motor PD into 11 symptom/functional domains encompassing 40 distinct standardized reported symptoms.
A single one-hour session of whole-body hyperthermia significantly reduced LC3-II autophagy marker levels in PBMCs from all nine ME/CFS patients.
At baseline, ME/CFS patients showed higher LC3-II autophagy marker levels than healthy donors.
Basal mitochondrial respiration in PBMCs increased significantly after one WBH session in all nine ME/CFS patients.
Mitochondrial ATP production in PBMCs increased significantly after WBH in ME/CFS patients.
Maximal mitochondrial respiration increased significantly after WBH in ME/CFS patients.
Spare respiratory capacity increased significantly after WBH in ME/CFS patients.
At baseline, ME/CFS patients trended toward higher basal respiration than healthy donors, though this did not reach statistical significance.
At baseline, ME/CFS patients trended toward higher ATP production than healthy donors, though not statistically significant.
Maximal respiration at baseline did not differ between ME/CFS patients and healthy donors.
Spare respiratory capacity at baseline did not differ significantly between ME/CFS patients and healthy donors.
ULK1 mRNA expression was essentially unchanged after WBH.
BECN1 mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH.
ATG7 mRNA expression was essentially unchanged after WBH.
MAP1LC3B mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH, consistent with it being an early-response gene to heat shock.
AMPK1α mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH.
SIRT1 mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH.
FOXO3 mRNA expression was essentially unchanged after WBH.
SOD2 mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH, with high inter-individual variability.
NDUFS1 mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH.
TFAM mRNA expression was essentially unchanged after WBH.
SIRT3 mRNA expression decreased after WBH, a change that approached but did not reach conventional statistical significance.
HSPA5 (BiP/GRP78, an HSP70 family member) mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH, consistent with a heat-shock response.
IL-10 mRNA expression showed a non-significant increase after WBH, interpreted by the authors as reflecting an immunomodulatory effect of hyperthermia.

Some patients self-reported symptomatic improvement after WBH, including fewer swollen lymph nodes, faster recovery after exertion, and greater ability to cope with stress and daily activities, though this was not captured with standardized instruments.
In an aggregate dataset of 2313 ME/CFS patients, 14.1% (N=327) met criteria for experiencing sleep reversal (sleeping during the day and staying awake at night), while 85.9% (N=1986) did not.

Among 54 DSQ symptoms assessed, 53 (all except sensitivity to alcohol) had significantly higher composite scores in the Sleep Reversal group compared to the No Sleep Reversal group, indicating markedly greater overall symptom burden.
Participants with sleep reversal scored significantly worse than those without sleep reversal on every SF-36 subscale, indicating greater functional impairment.

A random forest classification model using 15 selected features (oversampled for class imbalance) predicted sleep reversal status with a mean AUC 95% CI of 0.7643-0.7831 and overall accuracy of 74.46%.
Difficulty falling asleep, age, and BMI were the three most important features (by mean decrease in Gini) for predicting sleep reversal in the random forest model.
The Sleep Reversal group was significantly younger and had significantly higher average BMI than the No Sleep Reversal group, along with differences in marital and work status.

Four pain-related features (muscle pain, joint pain, soreness, and SF-36 pain subscale) were among the top 15 predictors of sleep reversal, suggesting a link between pain, inflammation, and sleep reversal in ME/CFS.

Three thermoregulation-related features (high temperature, feeling hot or cold for no reason, and sweating hands) were among the top predictors of sleep reversal, suggesting poorer thermoregulation possibly linked to inflammation in this subgroup.
Twitching was among the top predictors of sleep reversal, potentially reflecting an underlying restless leg syndrome-type movement disorder that disturbs nighttime sleep.

The paper hypothesizes that lower cortisol levels, linked to circadian rhythm misalignment, may contribute to pain and sleep difficulties underlying sleep reversal, based on prior findings of reduced cortisol excretion and its association with pain in ME/CFS.
Higher baseline concentrations of β2-adrenergic receptor autoantibodies were significant predictors of a lower (worse) EQ-5D-5L quality-of-life index score in a multilevel model.
Higher baseline concentrations of M3-muscarinic acetylcholine receptor autoantibodies were significant predictors of a lower (worse) EQ-5D-5L quality-of-life index score.
None of the four measured autoantibodies showed a statistically significant change in concentration after four sessions of plasmapheresis plus IVIG.
Repeated-measures ANOVA across T1, T2, and T3 revealed no statistically significant improvements in clinical outcomes (ISI, FSS, HADS, EQ-5D-5L) following plasmapheresis and IVIG therapy.
A non-significant trend toward improvement in health-related quality of life, as measured by the EQ-5D-5L index score, was observed over the course of plasmapheresis and IVIG treatment.

Most patients (5 of 7) reported subjective benefit after the first plasmapheresis plus IVIG session, but many experienced marked post-exertional deterioration ('crushes') after the second session, leading to premature therapy termination in three cases.
One of seven patients (14%) developed a catheter-related infection requiring premature removal of the central venous catheter used for plasmapheresis.

In a separate cited immunoadsorption study, ADRB2 autoantibody titers dropped a mean of 77% immediately after the fourth procedure but only 6–19% four weeks later, with no correlation between AAB levels and clinical response.

In a separate cited cohort of 27 long COVID patients treated with INUSpheresis, autoantibodies against β1- and β2-adrenergic receptors decreased by 33% and 28%, and against M3- and M4-muscarinic receptors by 48% and 39%, respectively, after two treatments.

In a separate cited retrospective case-control study of 30 long COVID patients (3 groups of 10), those receiving IVIG plus supportive treatment showed the greatest clinical benefit as measured by modified ISARIC scores, compared to inhaled glucocorticoids or supportive care alone.
Among reviewed potential PASC treatments, metformin (phase 2-3 RCTs) and low-dose naltrexone (large cohort studies) showed the strongest supporting evidence.

In a cited single-center prospective observational study of 1966 patients, administration of dexamethasone and remdesivir during acute COVID-19 was associated with a lower percentage of patients developing post-COVID-19 condition.

In a study of 80 subjects, some healthy individuals (SARS-CoV-2-naive and post-COVID healthy) exhibited higher GPCR autoantibody levels than symptomatic ME/CFS or post-COVID syndrome patients, suggesting AAB concentration alone is not pathognomonic.
Among the post-COVID syndrome/ME-CFS patient groups in the cited study, autoantibody concentrations positively correlated with symptom severity.
Autoantibody levels against the β2-adrenergic receptor and M4-muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (CHRM4) decreased in clinical responders to rituximab, suggesting a link to disease activity.

Elevated vasoregulatory GPCR autoantibodies correlated with fatigue and muscle pain in post-infectious ME/CFS patients, whereas non-infection-triggered ME/CFS patients showed fewer and distinct correlations.
Contrary to studies supporting an AAB-disease activity link, other researchers found no connection between autoantibody titers and ME/CFS disease activity.
Some researchers have raised concerns that microclots may not play a significant pathogenic role in ME/CFS, contradicting the hypothesis that plasma exchange benefits patients via microclot removal.

A cited retrospective review of 1219 plasma exchange treatments in 145 patients reported depletion coagulopathy in 47.6%, hypocalcemia in 44.1%, and hypokalemia in 36.6% of cases, without associated bleeding complications.

Previous studies report overall plasma exchange complication rates of 11–18%, with major complications (cardiovascular, respiratory, anaphylactoid reaction, hemorrhage, sepsis) occurring in 0.025–4.75% of sessions.
PEM scores were significantly higher in PCS and ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
SSS-8 somatic symptom burden scores were significantly higher in PCS and ME/CFS patients than healthy controls.
SSD-12 scores indicating psychological distress related to somatic symptoms were significantly higher in PCS and ME/CFS patients than in healthy controls.
PTSD, depression (PHQ), and anxiety (GAD-7) scores showed no significant differences between PCS, ME/CFS, and control groups.

Concentration impairment, processing difficulties, sensory overload, stress sensitivity, and headache were significantly more prevalent in PCS/ME-CFS patients than controls after multiple-testing correction.
Word-finding issues and the overall neurological and cognitive symptom category lost statistical significance after multiple-testing correction.
Elevated concentration of at least one bacterial uremic metabolite was more common in PCS patients than in controls or ME/CFS patients, though not statistically significant.
Elevated HPHPA levels above reference range were found exclusively in PCS patients, not in ME/CFS or controls.
Elevated hippuric acid levels were exclusively observed in PCS patients among the three cohorts.
Tryptamine levels were elevated in both PCS and ME/CFS patients but not in healthy controls, suggesting a potential shared biomarker for post-infectious syndromes.
Concentrations of all nine investigated bacterial uremic metabolites did not significantly differ between PCS, ME/CFS, and healthy control groups.

Indole-3-acetic acid and indoxyl sulfate levels were associated with fatigue and neurological symptoms across the study population, though this association did not survive multiple-testing correction.
TMAO and hippuric acid were associated with neuroendocrine abnormalities including temperature dysregulation and altered circadian rhythms, but this did not remain significant after correction.
P-cresol sulfate was associated with intestinal symptoms and dyspnea, suggesting possible gut-lung interactions, though not significant after correction.
Phenylacetylglutamine correlated with vertigo, suggesting a role in autonomic dysfunction, but the association did not remain significant after correction.
Sex distribution differed significantly across the Ctrl, PCS, and ME/CFS groups, with Ctrl and PCS predominantly female and ME/CFS predominantly male.
The 2021 NICE guideline for ME/CFS discourages graded exercise therapy (fixed incremental activity/exercise programs) because it risks worsening post-exertional malaise.

Cognitive-behavioural therapy, once positioned as a primary treatment for ME/CFS, is now recommended only as an adjunct supportive therapy to help patients cope, not as a means of curing the underlying illness.

The 2015 Institute of Medicine report redefined ME/CFS (proposing the term systemic exertion intolerance disease) with diagnostic criteria centered on post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive impairment, and orthostatic intolerance.
No drug has regulatory (e.g., FDA) approval for treating the fatigue of ME/CFS, and no specific pharmacotherapy is recommended for the fatigue symptom itself.
The NICE 2021 guideline lowered the minimum symptom duration required for an ME/CFS diagnosis from 6 months to 3 months, to allow earlier intervention.
A significant subset of patients with cancer-related fatigue also exhibit post-exertional malaise, a hallmark symptom of ME/CFS, suggesting meaningful clinical overlap between the two conditions.

ME/CFS pathophysiology is characterized by dysregulated immune, autonomic, and HPA-axis physiology, with post-exertional malaise reflecting an inability to tolerate physical or cognitive stress, and illness onset often triggered by infection or another stressor.

Neither the American Psychiatric Association nor the World Psychiatric Association has issued dedicated clinical guidelines for ME/CFS, leaving clinicians reliant on multidisciplinary consensus statements (e.g., NICE, IOM, EUROMENE).
A study found significantly reduced creatine levels in the anterior cingulate cortex of PVFS patients compared with healthy controls.
Skeletal muscle and brain creatine levels were substantially reduced in individuals with post-COVID fatigue syndrome, with lower creatine correlating with greater symptom severity.
Cerebral creatine depletion was confirmed in patients recovering from severe COVID-19, indicating profound metabolic disruption.
A six-month course of creatine monohydrate supplementation improved patient- and clinician-reported outcomes and enhanced brain and muscle bioenergetics in a small group of patients.
A three-month RCT combining creatine supplementation with breathing exercises reduced respiratory discomfort and improved cognitive function.
Additional non-randomized studies using daily creatine doses up to 16 grams reported benefits on fatigue, cognition, and tissue bioenergetics.
High-dose creatine monohydrate supplementation produced only a modest (<10%) increase in total brain creatine in most brain regions.
A non-creatine-based synbiotic mixture increased low brain creatine levels in PVFS patients, and these increases were associated with improved clinical outcomes.
Some studies in pulmonary rehabilitation populations similar to PVFS reported minimal or no significant effects of creatine supplementation, contrasting with other positive reports.
A hypometabolic state involving impaired sphingolipid abundance and reduced mitochondrial substrate oxidation may contribute to persistent energy imbalance in PVFS.

Bioinformatic screening identified 217 spermatogenesis-linked human proteins sharing 245 pentapeptide sequences (324 total occurrences) with the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein, suggesting molecular mimicry as a potential mechanism for fertility-related autoimmunity.
Serum IgG reactivity against peptide 2 (shared with testis-specific serine/threonine kinase 1) was significantly higher in long COVID-19 syndrome patients than in acute COVID-19 patients.

Peptide 4, which contains motifs shared with KMT2D and other oogenesis/placenta-linked proteins, showed the highest overall antibody reactivity among infected patients in both acute and long COVID-19 groups.
Women with long COVID-19 syndrome had significantly higher rates of anti-peptide 2 antibodies than women with acute COVID-19.
Men with acute COVID-19 showed only a non-significant trend toward higher anti-peptide 4 antibody levels compared to men with long COVID-19 syndrome.
Positivity for anti-peptide 2 and anti-peptide 4 antibodies was more common in older (>60 years) acute COVID-19 patients, whereas positive LCS patients tended to be younger.
Peptide-reactive antibody status showed no significant correlation with C-reactive protein, total IgG/IgM levels, or pre-existing classical autoantibodies (anti-dsDNA, anti-snRNP, anti-Ro/La).
No correlation was found between peptide-reactive antibodies and long COVID patients presenting or not presenting chronic fatigue syndrome, regardless of gender.

Long COVID-19 patients who developed chronic fatigue syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 infection had significantly higher levels of anti-peptide 2 and anti-peptide 4 antibodies than COVID-19-negative patients with idiopathic chronic fatigue syndrome.
Women infected by SARS-CoV-2 had significantly higher levels of anti-peptide 2 antibodies compared to women with idiopathic chronic fatigue syndrome.

Vaccination with either BNT162b2 (mRNA) or ChAdOx1 (adenoviral vector) COVID-19 vaccines did not induce the antibody reactivity pattern against Spike peptides 1-4 seen in naturally infected patients, at 1-3 months post-vaccination.
Affinity-purified mouse IgG antibodies raised against Spike-derived peptide 2 specifically bound antigens in mouse testicular tissue by immunohistochemistry, whereas control IgG showed no signal.
Purified mouse IgG antibodies against peptides 2 and 4 specifically bound the full-length recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein in western blot, confirming their cross-reactive specificity.
Immunization of healthy BALB/c mice with peptides 2 or 4 produced no macroscopic organ, tissue, or body cavity alterations, indicating no apparent toxicity from the peptides or induced antibodies.
A cited prior study found that 25.5% of COVID-19 recoverees exhibited oligo-crypto-azoospermia, substantially higher than the 1%-3% baseline rate in the general population.
ME/CFS diagnosis was reported as one of several 'diagnostic roadblocks' that clinicians conceptualised as comparable to mental health/psychosomatic conditions, contributing to delayed SLE diagnosis.
A patient diagnosed with ME in 2005 reported that this diagnosis prevented proper investigation of other symptoms, and she was not diagnosed with SLE until 2013, an 8-year gap.
Citing Cornet et al., the authors note an initial misdiagnosis of fibromyalgia was associated with a 5-year increase in median SLE diagnostic delay.
Fibromyalgia was frequently reported to be diagnosed without a full history or physical exam, contributing to its role as a diagnostic roadblock for SLE.

The authors note that early childhood trauma may be a shared risk factor for both fibromyalgia and SLE, raising the possibility that fibromyalgia could develop years before SLE onset rather than solely representing misdiagnosis.
Prior studies indicate a mean time to SLE diagnosis in the UK of 6 to 7 years from first symptom onset.

In contrast to the longer adult delays, Nightingale et al. found a median time to SLE diagnosis of only 6 months among 10-19 year olds with mild to moderate disease in the UK, indicating early diagnosis is achievable.
Neuro-psychiatric SLE symptoms are particularly susceptible to clinical misattribution, likely because clinicians underestimate the prevalence of neuro-psychiatric symptoms in SLE.
The majority of the 268 surveyed SLE patients reported multiple misattributions of their symptoms prior to receiving their SLE diagnosis.
Psychological/psychosomatic misattributions of SLE symptoms could persist even in the face of clear physical evidence, such as a patient with swollen legs being told she was suffering from anxiety.
Patients frequently reported 'moral misattributions' by clinicians, including being accused of exaggerating or faking symptoms, which undermined help-seeking and diagnosis.
Comparison of mean diagnostic journey length for patients diagnosed in different decades did not reveal any major differences in diagnostic delay over time.
Moxibustion at Zusanli (ST36) improved general condition scores and behavioral performance (Open Field Test, Exhaustion Treadmill Test, Morris Water Maze) in a rat model of chronic fatigue syndrome.
Comparison of hippocampal proteomes between control and CFS model rats identified 72 differentially expressed proteins (31 up-regulated, 41 down-regulated) associated with CFS development.

Comparison of hippocampal proteomes between moxibustion-treated and CFS model rats identified 103 differentially expressed proteins (40 up-regulated, 63 down-regulated) related to the therapeutic effects of moxibustion.
KEGG pathway enrichment analysis linked CFS pathogenesis in the hippocampus to base excision repair, steroid biosynthesis, and systemic lupus erythematosus pathways.
KEGG pathway analysis indicated that the therapeutic effect of moxibustion on CFS involved the terpenoid skeleton biosynthesis pathway.

Sixteen potential hippocampal biomarker proteins were identified whose expression changes in CFS were reversed by moxibustion (14 up-regulated proteins reduced, 2 down-regulated proteins restored), functionally linked to synaptic plasticity, ribosomal function, neurotransmitter secretion, glycine metabolism, and mitochondrial function.
GO enrichment analysis of hippocampal DEPs showed that both CFS and moxibustion treatment were associated with multiple biological processes, molecular functions, and cellular components.
KEGG pathway enrichment linked CFS pathogenesis in the hippocampus to the base excision repair pathway.
KEGG pathway enrichment linked CFS pathogenesis in the hippocampus to the steroid biosynthesis pathway.
KEGG pathway enrichment linked CFS pathogenesis in the hippocampus to the systemic lupus erythematosus pathway, suggesting an immune-related mechanism.
KEGG pathway enrichment showed that the therapeutic effect of moxibustion in CFS rats was relevant to the terpenoid skeleton biosynthesis pathway.
Sixteen potential hippocampal protein biomarkers were identified whose CFS-associated dysregulation (14 up-regulated, 2 down-regulated) was reversed by moxibustion treatment.

Sixteen hippocampal proteins were identified as potential biomarkers whose expression changes in CFS model rats were reversed by moxibustion treatment, including 14 that were up-regulated in CFS and reversed toward normal, and 2 that were down-regulated in CFS and reversed toward normal.
The 16 candidate biomarker proteins reversed by moxibustion were functionally categorized as being mainly involved in synaptic plasticity.
Among the 16 reversed candidate biomarkers, several were categorized as related to ribosomal function.
Among the 16 reversed candidate biomarkers, several were categorized as involved in neurotransmitter secretion.
Among the 16 reversed candidate biomarkers, several were categorized as related to glycine metabolism.
Among the 16 reversed candidate biomarkers, several were categorized as related to mitochondrial function.
The proteomics differential expression results were validated for reliability using Parallel Reaction Monitoring targeted mass spectrometry.
Pooled analysis of 4 studies showed exercise-based rehabilitation produced a small but statistically significant reduction in fatigue compared to control at short-term follow-up (≤3 months).
Exercise-based programs showed a small, non-significant improvement in physical functionality compared to control at short-term follow-up.
In the medium term (3-6 months), exercise-based programs produced a small but significant reduction in fatigue compared to control.
Exercise therapy did not improve physical functionality compared to conventional treatment in the medium term, with the pooled effect slightly favoring the control group.
In the long term (≥6 months), exercise programs did not show a significant effect on reducing fatigue compared to control treatments.
No significant improvements in physical functionality were observed with exercise programs compared to conventional treatment in the long term.
Methodological quality of the 11 included studies was generally moderate, with a mean PEDro score of 6.72/10, and none of the studies blinded both patients and therapists.

GRADE assessment rated the certainty of evidence for exercise-based rehabilitation's effect on fatigue and physical functionality in CFS as low to moderate, resulting in a weak recommendation favoring exercise.

In one included trial (PACE-type design), Graded Exercise Therapy (GET) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) showed significantly greater improvement than Specialist Medical Care (SMC) or Adaptive Pacing Therapy (APT) on fatigue outcomes at 52 weeks.

The review notes inconsistent reporting of adverse events across included exercise trials, limiting the ability to accurately assess safety of exercise-based rehabilitation in CFS, a population at risk of post-exertional malaise.
Patients with fibromyalgia/CFS scored significantly higher on the Need for Controllability and Predictability questionnaire (NCP-q) than healthy controls, with a large effect size.
The NCP-q showed excellent internal consistency when administered to the fibromyalgia/CFS patient subgroup.
Fibromyalgia/CFS patients did not differ significantly from patients with panic disorder, overstrain, or burnout on NCP-q scores, suggesting a shared transdiagnostic elevation in need for control.
An overall one-way ANOVA across panic disorder, overstrain, burnout, fibromyalgia/CFS, and healthy control groups showed a significant main effect of group on NCP-q total score.
Prior published research cited by the authors reported that a higher need for control is associated with both chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia.
In the student validation sample, the NCP-q total score correlated moderately and positively with intolerance of uncertainty (IUS), supporting convergent validity.
NCP-q total score correlated moderately and positively with worry severity (PSWQ) in the student validation sample.
NCP-q total score correlated moderately and positively with trait anxiety (STAI-T) in the student validation sample.
NCP-q total score correlated moderately and positively with depression severity (BDI-II) in the student validation sample.
Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses both supported a one-factor structure for the NCP-q, indicating it can be scored as a single dimensional construct.
The NCP-q demonstrated excellent internal consistency across the combined student sample.
The NCP-q showed acceptable test-retest reliability over a four-week interval in a subsample of students.

A man with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome developed cerebral air embolism, initially misdiagnosed as posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome based on MRI, with the correct diagnosis only revealed on closer inspection of the CT scan.

The paper highlights that CT scan scrutiny, rather than MRI, is key to correctly diagnosing cerebral air embolism, and that temporal proximity to procedures introducing air into circulation is an important diagnostic clue.

A novel heterozygous splice-site variant, COL12A1 c.8415+1G>A, was identified by whole-exome sequencing in both affected siblings of Family A and classified as likely pathogenic, predicted and confirmed by RNA analysis to cause skipping of exon 56 with an in-frame deletion in the COL2 domain.

A splicing variant, COL12A1 c.8319+1G>T, previously reported in ClinVar as pathogenic, was identified in the Family B proband and confirmed by RNA analysis to cause skipping of exon 55, resulting in an in-frame deletion in the COL2 domain.

Immunofluorescence of patient-derived skin and tendon fibroblasts showed a disorganized filamentous collagen XII network with spot-like aggregates, in contrast to the normal fibrillar pattern seen in control cells.
Western blot analysis showed increased collagen XII expression in both cell lysates and culture media of patient-derived fibroblasts compared to controls.

Collagen I and collagen VI protein expression were also significantly increased in lysates and secreted media of patient fibroblast cultures compared to unaffected controls, alongside collagen XII changes.
Secreted collagen XII from patient cultures showed an abnormal, slower migration pattern on Western blot, likely reflecting altered post-translational modification of the long α1(XII) isoform.

In Family A skin fibroblasts (COL12A1Δ56), collagen I and VI showed coarse fibrillar organization by immunostaining, whereas in Family B tendon fibroblasts (COL12A1Δ55) their organization was not significantly altered compared to controls.

The three new patients confirmed the combined mEDS phenotype of joint hypermobility (Beighton scores 5-6/9) together with neck, proximal, and distal muscle weakness (MRC 4/5), consistent with the previously described COL12A1-related myopathy phenotype.
Literature review identified 31 families with COL12A1-related myopathy/mEDS phenotype reported to date, 18 with autosomal dominant and 13 with autosomal recessive inheritance.

Muscle imaging shows that in COL12A1-related myopathy the muscle (e.g., rectus femoris) is variably reduced in size and surrounded by increased connective tissue (epimysium) thickness, distinct from the peripheral fibro-adipose replacement pattern seen in collagen VI-related myopathy.

Respiratory function is more severely compromised in the recessive UCMD2 form compared to UCMD1, with three of ten UCMD2 patients requiring non-invasive ventilation before age 3, versus onset near the end of the first decade in UCMD1.
Creatine kinase levels were normal in most COL12A1-RM patients across the literature and in the new patients, with only four BTHLM2 patients showing slight CK elevation.
Unenhanced CT in a patient with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome showed an abnormally elevated left hemidiaphragm.
Dynamic Digital Radiography during forced breathing revealed reduced excursion (impaired motility) of the left diaphragm compared to the right diaphragm in the same EDS patient.
Post-processing analysis of regional lung motility showed normal motility in the right lung but reduced motility in the left lung, with fewer and smaller motion vectors.

Unlike CT or MRI which provide detailed anatomy but no dynamic functional assessment, Dynamic Digital Radiography allows dynamic visualization of diaphragm excursion, speed, and symmetry during breathing.
The use of pulsed X-ray in DDR allows lower radiation exposure compared to fluoroscopy.
Pain intensity was significantly related to depressive symptoms and pain-related anxiety in patients with hEDS, with the strength of this relationship differing by anatomical region.
The strongest associations between depressive symptoms and pain intensity were found for pain located in the abdomen and lower extremities.
Pain in the upper extremities was not significantly related to either depressive symptoms or pain-related anxiety.
Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome results from mutations in the COL3A1 gene, which encodes type III collagen and leads to weakened connective tissue.
Patients with vascular EDS are at elevated risk for spontaneous arterial dissections, ruptures, aneurysms, and arteriovenous fistulas due to connective tissue fragility.

The patient with VEDS developed two iatrogenic arteriovenous fistulas in the distal left radial artery after blind (non-ultrasound-guided) radial arterial line placement during an endovascular splenic artery embolization procedure.

The two radial artery AVFs were ultimately managed with surgical ligation of the left radial artery using Hemoclips and transfixing Prolene suture, resulting in complete symptom resolution at one-month follow-up.

The authors recommend that ultrasound-guided Seldinger technique for arterial access, rather than blind cannulation, should be used systematically in VEDS patients to reduce iatrogenic vascular complications.

Unlike in the general population where iatrogenic AVFs often resolve spontaneously, this does not typically occur in VEDS patients, informing the decision for close monitoring rather than immediate intervention.
Parents of children with chronic pain conditions including Ehlers-Danlos syndrome/hypermobility reported frequent experiences of their child's pain being dismissed by healthcare professionals.

Parents described taking an active role in advocating for their child and encouraging communication about pain, identified as a key building block of effective pain communication with healthcare professionals.

Cytology of the dermal mass in a dog with cutaneous asthenia showed unusually numerous, pleomorphic spindloid (fibroblast) cells that raised concern for sarcoma, though this reflected reactive rather than neoplastic cells.
Histologic examination showed markedly haphazardly arranged dermal collagen forming wispy, curled strands within loose fibrous connective tissue containing plump reactive fibroblasts.
Compared to normal control skin, dermal elastin fibers were reduced in number and replaced by abnormal fine, haphazardly arranged fibers with occasional thick bands, on Verhoeff-Van Gieson staining.
The paper notes that mutations in COL5A1 are associated with classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in humans, and specific COL5A1 mutations have also been described in some dogs with cutaneous asthenia.

Dermal small-caliber blood vessels showed increased numbers with plump, reactive endothelium exhibiting anisokaryosis and occasional binucleation, consistent with a reactive/reparative vascular response in the affected skin.

Reactive fibroblast hyperplasia in cutaneous asthenia can be cytologically mistaken for neoplastic mesenchymal cells (sarcoma), which is an important diagnostic pitfall even though cytology itself cannot diagnose cutaneous asthenia.
Overexpression of disease-causing ACTA2 R179H or TGFBR2 G357W mutations in primary murine aortic VSMCs markedly reduced Pgc1α protein levels compared to control-transduced cells.
ACTA2 R179H and TGFBR2 G357W mutant VSMCs showed reduced Tfam protein levels along with decreased mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) content compared to controls.
Mitochondrially encoded respiratory complex IV subunits Mt-Co1 and Mt-Co2 protein levels were reduced in ACTA2 R179H and TGFBR2 G357W mutant VSMCs relative to controls.
